A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Grokking Finite-Dimensional Algebra. Their main text, equations, figures, and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original neural-network training experiments, representation probes, algebra-category comparisons, and rank/sparsity analyses in Section 5 and Appendix E.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and reports additional Transformer analyses and experiments on matrix and upper-triangular matrix algebras.

M1.justification: The structure-tensor learning framework, embedding-based model families, training objectives, and representation probe remain unchanged. V2's explicit explanation of ridge fitting in Section 5.2 describes a procedure already documented in v1 Appendix E.

E1.justification: V2 Figure 7 adds evaluations on M2(F3), of dimension 4, and UT2(F5), of dimension 3. These targeted additions cover associative, noncommutative, unital algebras absent from the original two-dimensional evaluation; matrix algebras in v1 were mathematical examples rather than reported experiments.

E2.justification: No competing baseline algorithm is added or removed. The additional Transformer plots investigate a model family already included in the framework, rather than introduce a separate method evaluated against a proposed algorithm.

E3.justification: The newly reported Transformer evaluations specify a two-layer, two-head encoder with width 64 and AdamW learning rate 0.001 in Appendix E. These add concrete experimental conditions; the retained MLP/LSTM settings, split construction, metrics, and probing protocol are unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 Figures 2(b), 3(b), and 8 extend the representation and training-dynamics analyses to Transformers, including differences across layers. Existing MLP/LSTM probes, single-entry perturbations, and rank/sparsity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report two repetitions per algebra-category/tensor/training-fraction combination and retain the appendix's mean-and-standard-deviation procedure for random-projection probes. V2 adds no new seed, repetition-count, confidence-interval, or significance reporting.

E6.justification: V2 adds Transformer learning/probing curves and generalization-delay results for the two matrix algebras. It newly reports nearly constant Transformer embedding-layer alignment despite improving test accuracy. Existing results, including the perturbation histogram's mean delay of 6,701, are retained.

T1.justification: V2 adds Proposition B.7 proving the minimum dimension of an associative, unital, noncommutative algebra is 3, and Proposition B.8 giving Lie-algebra tensor conditions with a proof. These extend supporting theory while retaining the core results. The new Lie criterion omits the additional alternation requirement needed in characteristic two.

C1.justification: The abstract and substantive conclusion retain the same central claims: the FDA framework subsumes group tasks, algebraic and tensor properties influence grokking, and generalization accompanies representation formation. The added evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: New Section 6 discusses the Transformer embedding-layer exception, proposes shared embedding/unembedding weights as an explanation, and explicitly limits the predominantly two-dimensional empirical scope. The existing sparsity-basis qualification and future-work discussion are retained.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-repository link in the introduction and documents Transformer depth, heads, width, initialization, and optimizer settings in Appendix E. Existing MLP/LSTM hardware and training details and PCA/ridge implementation information remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 replaces Liu et al.'s Grokking as compression citation with Towards understanding grokking and corrects the Stander discussion from S5/S6 to S5. Its new discussion relates the Transformer exception to prior representation-learning findings. Most other reference changes update metadata or consolidate duplicate citations.

P1.justification: V2 adds a Discussion and Limitations section, reorganizes introductory appendix explanations, introduces model-specific headings in Appendix E, and makes localized prose and notation edits. Most existing text and the main narrative sequence are retained.

P2.justification: V1 Figures 3 and 9 are combined into v2's opening Figure 1. The representation figures gain Transformer panels, and new Figures 7 and 8 display additional experiments. Existing plots are otherwise largely preserved and relocated, with expanded captions and localized layout changes.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens empirical support through the previously unrepresented algebra regime in Figure 7 and additional Transformer diagnostics. Section 6 and Appendix E improve transparency about scope, interpretation, and reproduction. These gains are qualified by the untested weight-sharing explanation and the characteristic-two gap in new Proposition B.8, which does not affect the reported odd-prime experiments.
